rationale: five11 is a tiny (1259 text bytes, 12 functions) bit-stream decoding benchmark whose hot loops (read_x_bits, read_11_bits, five11) make it runtime-sensitive, while its small size makes every byte of bloat proportionally visible; therefore SUB gets the strongest pull (cheap, correct, high diversity for arithmetic-heavy bit manipulation), SPLIT is favored on the multi-block functions (five11, main) since it is nearly free and amplifies FLA/SUB coverage, and FLA is the primary structural defense with a moderate runtime penalty so the selector applies it to the larger control-flow-dense functions rather than the tiny list helpers. BCF is deliberately down-weighted via high RuntimeCost (0.7) and SizeCost (0.8) because bogus blocks would explode a 361-byte function and tax the tight bit-reading loops, so it only triggers where features indicate non-hot, security-critical regions. IBR and ICALL carry elevated RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk since indirect branches and calls in inner loops cost disproportionate performance on this benchmark and its linked-list traversal (free_list2) is pointer-sensitive, while IGV is a mild complement (few globals in this program) kept at low risk so it can diversify data references without meaningful overhead. This combination maximizes control-flow and data-transform diversity where it is cheap, and throttles the expensive passes so total runtime and size overhead stay within acceptable bounds for a MultiSource benchmark while correctness risk remains uniformly low.
